items.title: Southeast Asians scale back spending as Iran war spillover persists
Iran prepares for late supreme leader's funeral
items.description: The funeral for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed on February 28, the first day of the US-Iran war, was initially delayed but is now set to begin on Saturday. The ceremonies are expected to draw between 15 and 20 million mourners.

items.title: What are US and Japanese soldiers doing in the middle of the Australian bush?
items.description: The BBC's Katy Watson explains why troops are training in remote Australia - a country not at war, thousands of kilometres from today's major conflicts.

items.title: Crimea back in play? Russia feels pain of Ukraine long-range strikes
items.description: A couple of weeks back, we asked if the tide was turning in Ukraine. Short version: a little with a disclaimer: it's hard cutting through the fog of war. items.description: Talel Abd al-Aal was one of three senior terror operatives confirmed killed by the IDF in the past week, along with another top PIJ commander and a Hamas arms smuggler The post ‘Have fun in hell’: IDF kills Islamic Jihad man who held Rom Braslavski hostage, abused him appeared first on The Times of Israel.

items.title: How severe is Russia’s energy shortage because of Ukrainian strikes?
items.description: Analysts say Russia's fuel crisis may affect its domestic economy, but the war in Ukraine will remain the priority.

items.title: 'It's The Only Thing They're Talking About': Far From Ukraine War, Russia Fuel Crisis Consumes Local Worries
items.description: There’s no gasoline for ambulances in one region. In another, they’ve suspended garbage pickup because there’s no fuel for trucks. There’s a robust black market where you can pay someone to hold your place in endless lines of drivers hoping to fill up cars. Russia’s gasoline crisis is deepening.

items.title: Will alleged crime ties damage Serbia's ruling party?
items.description: Pressure on President Aleksandar Vucic is growing as years of investigations into alleged links between the state and organized crime coincide with a gang war. Experts say the issue is eroding support within his base.

items.title: China Urges Ukraine, Russia to Resume Peace Talks
items.description: China called on Ukraine and Russia to resume peace negotiations "as soon as possible" during a UN Security Council meeting on Monday. Beijing also reiterated its support for an immediate ceasefire, saying the humanitarian consequences of the war continue to worsen and urging both sides to demonstrate the political will…

items.title: Iran war supercharges pivot to renewable energy
items.description: The Iran war and high oil and gas prices have supercharged the adoption of renewables and EVs worldwide. Global investors say these technologies make financial sense and increase energy security.

items.title: Media, 'i feriti dell'attentato nel Principato di Monaco sono ucraini'
items.description: Le Figaro: 'Tre membri di una stessa famiglia, uno dei genitori è un oligarca di Kiev'

items.title: In flare-up over Hormuz, a hint at US-Iran roller coaster to come
items.description: If the core U.S.-Iran dispute has long been Tehran’s nuclear program, the tit-for-tat strikes in the Strait of Hormuz make clear that control of the waterway is of immediate concern to both. Neither wants a resumption of full-scale war, yet threats are flying.

items.title: Russian War Veteran Reportedly Jailed After Threatening Armed Revolt Against Kremlin
items.description: Alexander Lunin drew widespread attention last week after claiming the Russian army would “turn its weapons against the Kremlin” unless Putin personally met with him to address the alleged abuse of soldiers by military commanders.
